solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Son gets refill to avoid retiring

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for son, as in family trees
to top up a glass is to refill it

explanation.surface: A son keeps topping up his drink so he doesn't have to leave the party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retiring' here means going to bed, not leaving work: to stop up is British for staying up late.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: staying up late rather than going to bed is to stop up, an informal British phrase.

clue.text: Play for time with weapon

parts.note: T is the usual abbreviation for time, as in physics formulas
a rifle is a firearm, a weapon

explanation.surface: Someone stalling for time while holding a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play for time' looks like one phrase meaning stall; only 'Play' is the definition, as in toying with something.
explanation.definitionFit: To trifle with something is to toy or play with it, treating it lightly; a verb synonym.

clue.text: Modification to pit lane shows promise

indicators.note: a modification is a change, so the letters of the following words are changed round

explanation.surface: A racing circuit's improvements to its pit lane look encouraging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is part of the fodder, not a link: TO PIT LANE gives exactly the nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone with promise has potential, a capacity to develop into something good.

clue.text: Settle sovereign on a draught horse

parts.note: a bird that settles on a branch perches there
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen, a sovereign

explanation.surface: Instruction to sit a monarch on top of a heavy carthorse.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Percheron is a large French breed of heavy horse used for pulling ploughs and carts.

clue.text: Prank creates leak? Put a plug in it!

indicators.note: put ... in it tells us to place one piece inside the leak just named
with Put, these words say the plug goes inside the word for leak

parts.note: a leak of gas or water is an escape
a plug is a piece of publicity, an advertisement or AD

explanation.surface: A joker causes a leak, and someone shouts to stop it with a plug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put a plug in it' reads as a plumber's fix, but the plug is publicity, a commercial puff, and 'it' points back to the leak.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an escapade is a reckless or mischievous adventure, a prank or caper.

clue.text: Passage leads right into bar

indicators.note: into says the letter goes inside the word for bar

parts.note: bar as a preposition means except, as in 'all bar one'

indicators.note: the word at the front leads, so only the opening letter of right is used

explanation.surface: A corridor that goes straight on into a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passage' looks like a corridor but is a piece of text; 'bar' looks like a pub but means except.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an excerpt is a short extract or passage taken from a book, film or piece of music.

clue.text: Archer invested originally in copper coins

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: in places that opening letter inside the two coin letters

parts.note: p (new penny) and d (old penny) are two coin abbreviations

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so only the opening letter of invested is used

explanation.surface: A bowman who sank his money into copper coins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'd' is the old British penny, from Latin denarius, and 'p' the decimal penny.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Cupid, the Roman god of love, is pictured as a winged boy shooting arrows, so an archer.

clue.text: Space traveller lacks a bit of essential equipment

indicators.note: lacks says that letter is missing from the word for space traveller

parts.note: a planet travels through space on its orbit

indicators.note: a bit of means just one letter, the opening one of essential

explanation.surface: An astronaut is short of a vital piece of kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Space traveller' suggests an astronaut; it is a planet, wandering through space.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: plant is the machinery and equipment used in an industrial process, as in plant hire.

clue.text: Neighbourhood detective's scrupulous

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector; the 's stands for 'is' and joins the pieces
scrupulous, exacting, means strict

explanation.surface: A local police detective is very careful about everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a district is an area of a town or country, a locality or neighbourhood.

clue.text: Goulash so rich it is celebrated

indicators.note: a goulash is a stew of mixed ingredients, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A Hungarian stew so rich it is famous.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a historic event is famous, important in history, so celebrated.

clue.text: President to get up, giving commendation

parts.note: to get something up is to raise it

explanation.surface: A president rises to pay someone a compliment.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: praise and commendation both mean expressed approval of someone.

clue.text: Bed of fluff found in public house

indicators.note: found in says the fluff sits inside the pub abbreviation

parts.note: PH is the map abbreviation for public house, a pub
lint is the fluff that gathers on clothes

explanation.surface: A bed full of fluff discovered in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bed' is not furniture but a base, the foundation layer on which something rests.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a plinth is the base or bed on which a statue or column stands.

clue.text: Liverpool FC's sharp winger

parts.note: Liverpool Football Club are nicknamed the Reds
a sharp taste is tart

explanation.surface: A quick-witted wide player for Liverpool football club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winger' is a football position here, but the answer is a bird, a creature with wings.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the redstart is a small songbird with a red tail, and any bird is a winged creature.

clue.text: As usual some letters are questionable

indicators.note: some letters says only part of the following words is used, a run lying inside them

explanation.surface: As always, a few letters look doubtful.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang: sus, short for suspicious or suspect, means dubious or questionable.

clue.text: With hindsight audit should include old-style goods

indicators.note: should include means the audit word takes the old-style word inside it

parts.note: to audit accounts is to inspect them
retro goods are made in the style of the past

explanation.surface: Looking back, the inspectors ought to have checked the vintage stock.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: looking back on events after they happened, with the benefit of hindsight.

clue.text: Alumnus and soldiers kept late after school. That's compulsory!

parts.note: OB is an old boy, a former pupil or alumnus
LI is Light Infantry, a body of soldiers
gated means confined to school or college as a punishment

explanation.surface: A former pupil and some troops are given detention, and there's no getting out of it.
explanation.walkthrough: To be gated, in British school and university slang, is to be confined to the premises as a punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone who is obligated is bound or compelled to do something, so it is compulsory.

clue.text: This spicy brew is for researcher

indicators.note: a brew is something mixed and stirred, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A spicy concoction meant for a scientist.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a physicist is a scientist who carries out research into matter and energy.

clue.text: Manager protects the number showing emaciation

indicators.note: protects means the boss word wraps around the number like a shield

parts.note: a manager is a boss
nine is a number

explanation.surface: A boss shields the head count from showing how lean the firm is.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: emaciation is extreme thinness where the bones show through the skin.

clue.text: Basin in the kitchen where one might hear pins drop

definitions.text: where one might hear pins drop

parts.note: a basin is a bowl
a galley is the kitchen on a ship or aircraft

explanation.surface: A mixing bowl in the kitchen, so quiet you could hear a pin drop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hear a pin drop' means silence, but here the pins are skittles knocked down by a ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: at a ten-pin venue the skittles, called pins, are knocked down by the ball.

clue.text: One needs divinity for exasperation

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
RE is religious education, the school subject of divinity

explanation.surface: A person who needs God to cope with their annoyance.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: ire is anger, and exasperation is intense irritation.

clue.text: A couple's contract

parts.note: to couple is to join, as a bridge joins; the 's stands for 'is' and links to the definition

explanation.surface: A marriage agreement drawn up for two partners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contract' looks like a noun for an agreement but is a verb, to shorten.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to abridge a text is to shorten or condense it, so to contract it.

clue.text: Drives bullocks

definitions.meaning: guides a vehicle by working the wheel
young bulls that have been castrated, raised for beef

explanation.surface: A cattle drover moving young bulls along.
explanation.definitionFit: Homograph: one spelling is both a verb for guiding a car and the noun for castrated young bulls.

clue.text: One of the audience let siren off

indicators.note: off means gone wrong or bad, so these letters are spoiled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone at a concert sets off a siren.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a member of a radio or concert audience is one who hears, a hearer.

clue.text: Conviction for oriental living in mobile home

indicators.note: living in means sitting inside the home word

parts.note: a tent is a home you can carry about
E is short for east, so oriental

explanation.surface: A sentence handed to an Eastern traveller who lives in a caravan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conviction' suggests a court verdict but means a firmly held belief.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a tenet is a principle or belief firmly held, a conviction.

clue.text: Sister to dash back to Kent

indicators.note: back means the word for dash is read backwards

parts.note: to dash is to run
Kent is a county in South-East England, SE

explanation.surface: A sibling must hurry home to the county of Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is an English county in the south-east, hence SE. 'Sister' is a senior hospital nurse in British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: British usage: a sister is a senior hospital nurse in charge of a ward.

clue.text: Fellow holds the Italian tenor culpable

indicators.note: holds says the word for fellow wraps around the next pieces

parts.note: a fellow is a guy
il is the Italian for the
T is the abbreviation for tenor in music

explanation.surface: A man restrains an Italian opera singer who is to blame.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: being culpable means deserving blame, responsible for wrongdoing.

clue.text: More enthusiastic mourner

definitions.meaning: a person paid to wail at funerals, especially in Ireland

explanation.surface: A mourner who is more zealous than the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Homograph: the comparative of keen, and the noun for one who keens, wailing for the dead.

clue.text: I ntricate — like Three Blind Mice?

definitions.meaning: in the nursery rhyme the farmer's wife cut off the mice's tails

explanation.surface: A puzzling comparison between complexity and a nursery rhyme.
explanation.walkthrough: In the nursery rhyme the farmer's wife cuts off the mice's tails, so they are de-tailed.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: elaborate and full of particulars, and read as de-tailed, having had tails removed.

clue.text: Wears tie loosely, so to speak

indicators.note: something loosely arranged is not in its proper order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man who wears his necktie loose, in a manner of speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: both phrases flag that words are used figuratively, not literally.

clue.text: Abhor English international supporting Germany

indicators.note: in an across clue, supporting means coming after the word for Germany

parts.note: D is the international vehicle code for Germany
a test match is an international cricket fixture

explanation.surface: Someone hates an England cricketer who backs the German side.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to detest something is to loathe or abhor it.
